operations.detail: Queue, same-owner lease, stale canonical runner and absent runtime outputs were re-read from remote.
The uploaded 046 note conflicts with remote state and requests a parallel child; remote queue remains authoritative and parallel runner creation stays forbidden.
A checkpoint could previously resume when table row count matched even if row content changed.
Each checkpoint now stores and verifies a SHA-256 over all ordered table rows and required columns.
Existing checkpoints without a table fingerprint are invalidated and rebuilt instead of trusted.
UPRN or postcode mutations with unchanged row count produce a fingerprint mismatch and rebuild.
A UPRN with several same-source postcodes could previously reach common-table insertion and abort before a structured blocker report.
Common rows are generated only for UPRNs with exactly one distinct postcode in each source and the same postcode across NSUL and ONSUD.
Ambiguous UPRNs are counted as conflicts and excluded without raising a PRIMARY KEY exception.
Same-count mutation, legacy checkpoint, ordered hash and multi-postcode fixtures passed local preflight.
Canonical totals were recalculated from actual suites: 74 serial steps, 594 tests and 82 source checks.
Official hashlib, SQLite ORDER BY and WITHOUT ROWID contracts were bound to deterministic checkpoint fingerprints.
Queue references current checkpoint worker, tests, pipeline, manifest and registry blob SHAs.
Lease was renewed for the identical owner/session; no takeover or new runner occurred.
Four runtime checkpoint fingerprint rows and six concrete examples were published to the web layer.
Revision 18.6 registry and checkpoint plan increased the prepared artifact matrix to 65 entries.
No fingerprint runtime verification, hydrated package, exact join candidate or business row is claimed.
